payoff: Peta jalur POST /transfers end-to-end lalu diagnosis enam failure tanpa mengarang HTTP status ketika koneksi belum terbentuk.
learningOutcomes: gambarkan perjalanan POST /transfers dari client ke backend, tunjukkan layer & komponen yang memprosesnya; klasifikasikan 6 skenario failure berdasarkan layer.
mentalModel: HTTP defines request meaning, TCP transports an ordered byte stream for HTTP/1.1, IP forwards datagrams and Ethernet delivers across a local link; failures at lower layers may prevent any HTTP response.
relationshipGraph: Client → DNS (jika hostname) → TCP/IP path → router/firewall → optional L7 proxy/load balancer → backend HTTP handler → HTTP response or transport failure.

concepts.title: TCP/IP dan model lapisan
concepts.mechanism: Layering separates link, internet, transport and application responsibilities without making each a separate implementation process.

concepts.title: IPv4 routing, TCP dan encapsulation
concepts.mechanism: The outbound HTTP/1.1 request is carried by TCP segments inside IP packets over local frames; routers forward packets between links.

concepts.title: Klasifikasi failure berdasar boundary
concepts.mechanism: An HTTP response has a status code; pre-HTTP transport/network failures have other observations. HTTP intermediaries may emit responses.

misconceptions: OSI model is a diagnostic abstraction, not proof that every request uses TCP.
ECONNREFUSED and HTTP 503 are not interchangeable observations.
A normal IP router should not be confused with an L7 HTTP proxy.
practice: Separate a route failure from an HTTP response.
Run the Node fixture and explain the three output lines.

segments.objective: Explain the role of each boundary in an HTTP request without mistaking an OSI diagram for a wire trace.
segments.whyItMatters: When POST /transfers fails, a status code exists only if some HTTP component replies. The first task is to locate the boundary of failure.
segments.firstAction: Draw four boxes in order: HTTP application, TCP transport, IP internet, and Ethernet link; add one arrow for outgoing data.
segments.mentalModel: The layers are a reasoning map: HTTP supplies request meaning; TCP supplies a byte-stream connection in this example; IP selects packet delivery toward a destination; a local link carries frames toward the next hop.
segments.explanation: RFC 1122 describes link, internet and transport layers, with application protocols above them. The model is useful but not an implementation mandate. This lesson uses HTTP/1.1 over TCP/IPv4/Ethernet as a bounded example. HTTPS adds security and HTTP/3 uses a different transport; therefore this stack must not be universalized.

workedExample.problem: A browser or CLI posts a JSON transfer to api.example.test via an HTTP/1.1 origin.

steps.action: Label the request POST /transfers and the intended HTTP target.
steps.reason: The method and target identify application semantics.
steps.expectedResult: HTTP is the application-layer message, not a router command.

steps.action: Add TCP, then IP, then Ethernet below HTTP for the outbound request.
steps.reason: Each layer transports the payload of the layer above in this example.
steps.expectedResult: The outgoing stack reads HTTP → TCP → IPv4 → Ethernet.

steps.action: Reverse the order on the receiving host.
steps.reason: The receiver removes lower-layer framing before parsing the application message.
steps.expectedResult: The inbound stack reads Ethernet → IPv4 → TCP → HTTP.

guidedPractice.prompt: A diagram labels HTTP as the protocol that selects a router's next hop. Which box should be responsible for route selection?
hints: Look for the header with destination IP information.
Router forwarding decisions are principally at the internet layer.
guidedPractice.explanation: Internet-layer routing uses IP addressing. HTTP defines request semantics after a transport path is available.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Assuming every request uses HTTP over TCP and every network precisely implements a seven-layer OSI stack.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: OSI is a reference model; real stacks combine responsibilities. HTTP/3, for example, is not HTTP/1.1 over TCP.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Label the diagram 'HTTP/1.1 over TCP/IPv4 on Ethernet' and draw only the layers used by that scenario.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: Your drawing has HTTP→TCP→IP→Ethernet for outbound encapsulation and the inverse on the receiver.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Check whether you are mixing the direction of sending with how inbound frames are decapsulated.

independentChallenge.prompt: For an HTTP/1.1 GET /health call over a local wired link, draw the same stack and say where a TCP setup failure would occur.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: A different method and endpoint with an explicit connection-setup failure.
expectedEvidence: A correctly labelled stack and a transport-level failure, not an invented 500 status.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Trace how the IP packet traverses a router without assuming the Ethernet frame remains unchanged.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Start by naming the direction of encapsulation for HTTP/1.1 over TCP/IP.

segments.objective: Trace the client, router and server roles for POST /transfers and explain what changes at a hop.
segments.whyItMatters: A transfer request can fail before it arrives at the backend. Looking only at the controller hides the router or TCP boundary.
segments.firstAction: Write Client → Router → Server and mark the destination IP that each routing decision concerns.
segments.mentalModel: A router forwards IPv4 datagrams using IP addressing; the frame that carries an IP packet is scoped to a link. A TCP session is maintained by communicating endpoints, not by every intermediate router.
segments.explanation: RFC 791 describes IP datagrams, addresses and routing through gateways. RFC 9293 defines connection state and data transport at the endpoints. In common Ethernet routing, a frame is replaced on each hop even though the routed packet continues toward its IP destination; NAT or gateways can also transform headers. A packet may be dropped before any HTTP code runs.

workedExample.problem: POST /transfers travels across one IPv4 router to a remote API.

steps.action: Show a client choosing a destination IP and next hop.
steps.reason: An IP packet must be directed toward a host reachable through a network path.
steps.expectedResult: IP destination identifies the target origin or gateway, not the HTTP path /transfers.

steps.action: Draw a new link frame for the router's outgoing interface.
steps.reason: Ethernet delivery is local to each directly connected link.
steps.expectedResult: A frame addresses the next hop; the router forwards the IP datagram.

steps.action: Show the server TCP endpoint receiving bytes and its HTTP handler parsing the request.
steps.reason: TCP delivers a stream to the server endpoint; only an HTTP participant interprets the method and target.
steps.expectedResult: POST /transfers is interpreted at the receiving HTTP server or intermediary.

guidedPractice.prompt: At a router, which should guide normal IPv4 forwarding: the HTTP URL /transfers or the packet destination address?
hints: A conventional IP router need not parse HTTP to select an outgoing interface.
Look for the field present in the IP header.
guidedPractice.explanation: IP forwarding uses addressing and routing; HTTP path selection belongs to HTTP endpoints or L7 intermediaries.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Assuming the destination MAC address stays constant from client to remote backend.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: Ethernet addresses are scoped to one link; routers rewrite link framing for the next interface.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Redraw one frame on each hop while maintaining the higher-level request narrative.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: Your path labels client, router and server with IP forwarding and per-hop Ethernet framing.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Verify that you did not place HTTP request parsing on a normal IP router.

independentChallenge.prompt: Add an L7 reverse proxy before the backend and explain which component may now read HTTP /transfers.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: A proxy is introduced between the client and origin rather than pure IP forwarding.
expectedEvidence: Router versus HTTP proxy responsibilities are distinguished in the drawing.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Classify failures by whether a full HTTP response was received or no connection could be established.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Recall that IP forwarding and application-level proxying inspect different information.

segments.objective: Classify six request failures by boundary and produce an observable diagnostic for each.
segments.whyItMatters: A remote API can be broken in several ways. Treating all failures as HTTP 500 wastes incident-response time and may hide network exposure or readiness issues.
segments.firstAction: Label a 503 HTTP response separately from ECONNREFUSED and write what each one proves.
segments.mentalModel: An HTTP status is an application-protocol message received from an origin or intermediary. A DNS, link, routing or TCP setup failure can stop the exchange before any HTTP response exists.
segments.explanation: A practical six-case taxonomy is: (1) name lookup fails, (2) link/neighbor reachability fails, (3) IP route unavailable, (4) firewall policy blocks the flow, (5) TCP listener refuses the connection, and (6) an HTTP component returns a 5xx response. Cases 1–5 are not automatically HTTP responses; a gateway might generate an HTTP error on behalf of a failed upstream, so record who emitted the status. Use DNS tools, route/interface inspection, firewall policy/logs, listener checks and HTTP response inspection as distinct evidence. The bundled Node fixture verifies only locally generated 201/503 responses versus a refused TCP connection; it does not emulate DNS, routing, or network firewalls.

workedExample.problem: A local Node HTTP endpoint returns 201 on /transfers, 503 on /unavailable, then stops listening.

steps.reason: The fixture starts a loopback server on an operating-system-assigned port and sends real HTTP requests.

steps.action: After the server closes, try a fresh TCP request to the same port.
steps.reason: Without a listener the connection is refused before any HTTP response can exist.

steps.action: Categorize each output as HTTP or transport.
steps.reason: A numeric status code implies HTTP response handling; ECONNREFUSED is a connection error.
steps.expectedResult: Both status lines are HTTP responses; connect-error is not one.

guidedPractice.prompt: A CLI prints ECONNREFUSED when POSTing /transfers. Which layer should be investigated before debugging HTTP status handling?
hints: Did a response status code ever arrive?
Inspect the TCP listener and its bind address first.
guidedPractice.explanation: Connection refusal means no accepting listener at that address/port, or an active reject; there is no HTTP status to inspect yet.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Reporting a 503 when the TCP connection was refused.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: 503 requires an HTTP response from an HTTP origin or intermediary. A failed transport connection has no HTTP response.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Record the observed error string or status and name which component generated it.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: The fixture prints two HTTP status lines and one ECONNREFUSED transport error.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Check that Node supports the built-in http module and that the script is run without modifying its server lifecycle.

independentChallenge.prompt: Diagram six failures on a POST /transfers journey, adding one diagnostic observation and owning boundary for each. Include a reverse proxy that emits 502 when its upstream fails.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: Go beyond the loopback fixture to separate name resolution, a routed network, an intermediary and a backend failure.
expectedEvidence: Six distinct scenarios, appropriate investigation layer, and a clear distinction between an HTTP 502 and a transport refusal.
A cross-domain POST /transfers diagram showing client, router, firewall, proxy or LB, and server.

continueFromHere.resumeCue: Restart with the difference between an HTTP 503 response and a transport ECONNREFUSED error.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Dalam contoh HTTP/1.1 melalui TCP/IPv4/Ethernet, urutan encapsulation saat client mengirim pesan adalah?
reviewQuestions.explanation: HTTP adalah payload yang dibawa TCP, TCP dibawa IP, dan IP dibawa frame link lokal.
reviewQuestions.whenIncorrect: Jangan tertukar dengan decapsulation pada sisi penerima.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Apa yang biasanya digunakan router IPv4 untuk keputusan forwarding biasa?
options: Alamat tujuan IP dan routing table
reviewQuestions.explanation: Routing menggunakan alamat IP, bukan URL HTTP. Proxy L7 berbeda dari router biasa.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Client menerima ECONNREFUSED tanpa status HTTP. Diagnosis pertama yang paling kuat adalah?
options: Koneksi TCP ke alamat/port ditolak sebelum mendapat respons HTTP
reviewQuestions.explanation: ECONNREFUSED bukan respons HTTP; periksa listener, bind address dan policy jaringan.
reviewQuestions.whenIncorrect: Kode HTTP hanya ada jika HTTP component benar-benar mengirim response.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Apa arti hasil http-unavailable=503 di fixture lokal?
reviewQuestions.explanation: 503 adalah status HTTP yang dikirim server; berbeda dari kegagalan koneksi.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Reverse proxy mengembalikan HTTP 502 saat backend tak bisa dihubungi. Mana yang benar?
options: Client mendapat respons HTTP dari intermediary; penyebab upstream perlu diperiksa
Router IPv4 biasa pasti membuat HTTP 502
Seluruh perangkat di jalur menjalankan HTTP controller
reviewQuestions.explanation: Intermediary HTTP bisa menghasilkan responsnya sendiri meskipun origin tidak mengirim respons.
reviewQuestions.whenIncorrect: Pisahkan lokasi asal status yang diterima client dari root cause yang ada di upstream.
